howToUse.title: How to Use
howToUse.media:
• Add video or image URLs to build a playlist

• Configure the URL of the web page to display
• Set a secure PIN code
• Enable "Lock Mode" for full kiosk mode
• Tap 5 times on the secret button to access settings (default: bottom-right)
• Enter PIN code to unlock

lockMode.enableHint: Prevent users from exiting the kiosk app. Requires PIN code to exit.
lockMode.disabledWarning: With Lock Mode disabled, users can exit the app normally
lockMode.screenPinningInfo: Screen pinning enabled: Only 5-tap gesture + PIN code allows exit

lockMode.externalAppNoOwnerError: Device Owner required: Lock Mode will not work in External App mode without Device Owner privileges.
lockMode.externalAppOwnerInfo: Lock Mode enabled: Only 5-tap anywhere on screen + PIN code allows exit from external app
lockMode.blockPowerMenuHint: When enabled, long-pressing the power button has no effect — it can only turn the screen on/off with a short press. When disabled, long-pressing shows the power menu (Restart/Shutdown). Blocking the power menu may cause audio to be muted on some Samsung/OneUI devices.
lockMode.allowNotificationsHint: Enable notification dispatch to allow NFC tag reading in external apps. Note: Android will show the Home button (non-functional) and make the notification panel accessible when this is enabled.
lockMode.showSystemInfoHint: Displays the native Android status bar (time, battery, connectivity) in the locked app. This also fixes audio being muted on some Samsung/OneUI devices in lock mode.
lockMode.blockFactoryResetHint: Removes the 'Factory reset' option from the system Settings app (Device Owner restriction). Useful when the Settings app is on your multi-app whitelist, so locked users can't wipe the device. Persists across reboots. Takes effect immediately, even outside Lock Mode.
lockMode.allowRemoteScreenshotsHint: Lock Mode blocks screen capture device-wide (Power+Volume Down), which also blocks the REST /api/screenshot and cloud screenshot commands from capturing an app other than FreeKiosk (multi-app mode). Enable this to let FreeKiosk lift that block for the fraction of a second a remote capture takes, then restore it. Requires the FreeKiosk accessibility service and Android 11+.
lockMode.remoteScreenshotWarning: While a remote screenshot is being taken, the hardware screenshot combo is briefly available to anyone in front of the device.

autoLaunch.title: Auto Launch
autoLaunch.launchOnBootHint: Automatically launch FreeKiosk when the device starts
autoLaunch.appearOnTopInfo: Make sure "Appear on top" permission is enabled in system settings for reliable auto-launch.
autoLaunch.screenLockCompatHint: Enable ONLY if you set a native Android screen-lock (PIN/password) on this device. FreeKiosk then (1) steps aside for the secure lock screen at boot instead of locking immediately — preventing the reboot freeze caused by the conflict between the kiosk and the secure lock screen — and (2) keeps the system keyguard active while pinned, so the screen-lock actually prompts after the screen turns off and back on (without this, lock-task mode disables the keyguard and the password never appears). A system screen-lock means someone must enter the password on the device after every reboot before the kiosk starts, and on every wake — unsuitable for unattended devices. For device security, the FreeKiosk exit PIN + Device Owner is usually the better choice.
autoLaunch.screenLockCompatWarning: With a native screen-lock set, the device will require the password to be entered manually after every reboot before FreeKiosk launches. This has no effect unless an Android screen-lock is actually configured.
autoLaunch.defaultLauncherHintOwner: Makes FreeKiosk the persistent Home app via Device Owner. The system then relaunches FreeKiosk by itself after every reboot and system update, without relying on the OEM 'Appear on top' / Autostart permissions that some brands (e.g. Samsung) reset on OS updates — the main cause of the kiosk dropping out after a reboot/update. The Home button also returns here. Turning this off restores your normal launcher.
autoLaunch.defaultLauncherHintNonOwner: Opens the system Home-app picker so you can set FreeKiosk as the default launcher. The system then relaunches FreeKiosk at boot. Without Device Owner this choice is not locked — the user can change it back and some brands may reset it on a system update (Device Owner makes it permanent).
autoLaunch.defaultLauncherWarningOwner: FreeKiosk becomes the device Home/launcher. If the app were to crash on launch there is no fallback launcher, so test on one device before fleet rollout. Disabling this (or removing Device Owner) restores the normal launcher.
autoLaunch.defaultLauncherWarningNonOwner: Pick FreeKiosk in the Home-app screen that opens. This is not enforced without Device Owner and may be reset by a system update. To remove it later, choose another launcher in the same system screen.

camera.label: Camera
camera.description: Required for QR scanning, screenshots via camera and motion detection.

location.label: Location
location.description: Lets the cloud geolocate the device and report Wi-Fi details.

accessibility.label: Accessibility service
accessibility.description: Suppresses the back button and gestures to keep the kiosk locked down.

overlay.label: Display over other apps
overlay.description: Needed for blocking overlays and the status-bar guard.

usage.label: Usage access
usage.description: Lets FreeKiosk detect and relaunch the foreground app in external-app mode.

battery.label: Ignore battery optimizations
battery.description: Keeps the cloud heartbeat alive so the device can be woken remotely.

blockingOverlays.title: Blocking Overlays

Block touch input on specific areas of external apps. Useful for hiding
navigation bars, toolbars, or other interactive elements.

blockingOverlays.touchLoggerHint: Shows coordinates when you tap (30s countdown)

blockingOverlays.tip2: Percentage-based coordinates automatically adapt to screen rotation and different device sizes.
blockingOverlays.tip3: Regions can overlap. The return button will always stay accessible above blocking overlays.

The update has been downloaded successfully. The installation screen should appear shortly.

• Check notification panel
• Look for "Package installer"
• Grant installation permission if prompted

The update was downloaded but cannot be installed.

Please enable "Install from unknown sources" for FreeKiosk in your device settings, then try again.

On restricted devices (e.g. Echo Show), use:
adb install -r <apk>
